facts.heading: Did you know?
fact.1: An adult's body is about 50 to 60 percent water.
fact.2: The brain is roughly three quarters water.
fact.3: About 71 percent of the Earth's surface is covered by water.
fact.4: Only about 2.5 percent of the water on Earth is fresh water – and most of that is locked up in glaciers and ice.
fact.5: Water is densest at about 4 °C. That's why lakes freeze from the top down.
fact.6: Ice is about 9 percent lighter than liquid water, so it floats.
fact.7: About a fifth of the water we take in every day comes from food.
fact.8: The European Food Safety Authority (EFSA) suggests about 2 litres of water a day for women and 2.5 litres for men – drinks and food combined.
fact.9: Losing as little as about 2 percent of your body weight in water can noticeably reduce concentration and performance.
fact.10: Your kidneys filter around 180 litres of blood plasma every day – and the body takes almost all of it back.
fact.11: Even without sweating, you lose about half a litre to a litre of water a day through breathing and your skin.
fact.12: Thirst often only kicks in once your body is already a little short of fluid. Drinking regularly beats waiting.
fact.13: Water occurs naturally on Earth in all three states: as ice, as liquid and as vapour.
fact.14: On the summit of Mount Everest, water boils at only about 70 °C because of the low air pressure.
fact.15: In normal amounts, coffee and tea count towards your fluid intake too.
fact.16: Blood plasma is more than 90 percent water.
fact.17: Cucumbers and watermelons are more than 90 percent water.
fact.18: The sense of thirst often weakens with age – older people in particular should drink consciously.
fact.19: Water conducts heat about 25 times better than air. That's why you cool down so much faster in water.
fact.20: A water molecule consists of two hydrogen atoms and one oxygen atom: H₂O.
